subject: Several questions (switching from Mplus to Lavaan)

messages.subject: Several questions (switching from Mplus to Lavaan)
parts:
Hi guys, 

I want to run models I previously ran in Mplus in Lavaan, and struggle with a few points. Maybe you can help me out. Tried to google those problems and read the tutorials, but I didn't find help there. I'm sure I have missed some explanations. Please feel free to point me to them if you know about them.

1) I'm running a CFA with 30 ordinal items (scale 0,1,2,3). I define them as ordered in R, and use estimator="WLSMV" (this is the standard estimator for ordinal variables in Mplus). Now, what does the "Robust" estimation exactly mean here? In all my models the model fit of the Robust estimation (right column) is dramatically worse than the DWLS estimator (left column). 

2) If I use estimator = "MLR", it shows "ML" and "Robust" (left and right column again), but both estimations are 99% identical in my models. Does ML mean MLR here in this case? If so, what does Robust stand for? And if both are MLR, why are they sometimes a little bit different?

3) Where do I find the eigenvalues or explained R^2 by latent factors in the CFA? Is that the last line of the summary(fit) output, "F1   0.261    0.031" (F1 is the one CFA factor, I assume this means 26% R^2?).

4) I'm also trying to test longitudinal measurement invariance in various datasets and instruments, using the "longInvariance" command (semTools & Lavaan). It takes forever using MLR (50 times as long as Mplus), and with WLSMV it doesn't run at all. I receive the error (in all models and datasets):

longInvariance(QIDS.inv.model, auto=1, constrainAuto=TRUE, varList=constrainedVar, data=data1, estimator="WLSMV")
Error in crossprod(Delta[[g]], lavsamplestats @WLS.VD[[g]] * diff) : non-conformable arguments


Thanks for the help, and happy holidays :)
  Eiko

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Several questions (switching from Mplus to Lavaan)
parts:
Hi Eiko,

(1 & 2)

Robust estimators are not applied to point estimates, just to SE estimates and the chi-square test statistic.  In other words, the first step in MLR is to just run regular ML to get the point estimates (which is what you see in the summary() output), then the data's characteristics are used to adjust the usual SE/fit estimates so they have closer-to-nominal performance.  Using MLR, the left column is the regular fit statistic you would see if you just used estimator = "ML", and the right column is after the robust corrections are applied (i.e., the only output you see in Mplus when using MLR).  Same with WLSMV: the left column is using DWLS with no robust corrections for the fit statistic, and the right column is after applying the robust correction (so the right column is the one you want to pay attention to, even if it's bad news).  Here is a great paper explaining these and other robust corrections in SEM:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2013.824793

I think Yves has answered this question before, and provided a different source article for DWLS and robust differences, so try searching "DWLS robust" keywords at the top of the lavaan Google Group page.


(3) 

You can get R-squared for any outcomes (e.g., observed indicators, endogenous latent factors) by requesting it in the summary(), or using the inspect() function:

summary(fit, rsquare = TRUE)
inspect(fit, "rsquare") 

(4) 

I'm not sure how long you mean by "forever", but Mplus will generally be faster than lavaan because lavaan is written completely in R (not a programming language like C or Fortran).  It might take especially long if you have a large sample size, lots of missing data, or other things that make a model take a bit more time to converge.

semTools currently only has functions measurementInvariance (across groups for continuous indicators), measurementInvarianceCat (across groups for ordinal indicators), and longInvariance (across time, and potentially groups as well, for continuous indicators of only a single factor).  There is room for further development in all of these functions, but for right now, you'll just need to specify your few models and run them manually to test longitudinal invariance with ordinal indicators.

Terry

Dear Terry, 

Thank you so much for the very insightful reply! All problems solved. 

I will have to read up a bit more on the difference between WLSMV and DWLS, and the mimic="Mplus" option in Lavaan -- it would be good to get the same results. Bengt mentioned that the estimators differ in their "asymptotic approximations in estimating the asymptotic covariance matrix of the estimated sample statistics used to fit the model (i.e. the weight matrix)", but that results should be fairly similar in large samples.
